title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 (Corvinus): absolute reprobation blocks public prayers offered with due faith that the Word will profit all hearers
pass_a_gloss: Those do not rightly explain the doctrine of reprobation, who establish such a reprobation as would hinder that public prayers cannot be offered unto God with due faith and confidence that they will be profitable unto all hearing the word of God. For who can bring it into his mind that he should pray for the salvation of those whom God by an everlasting and antecedent will has willed to damn? The Apostle with this argument sharpens us unto praying for all, because God wills all to be saved.
pass_b_english: They do not rightly explain reprobation who set such a reprobation as would block public prayers from being offered to God with due faith and confidence that the Word will profit all who hear it. Who can bring himself to pray for the salvation of those God by an eternal antecedent will has willed to damn? The Apostle sharpens us to pray for all with this argument: God wills all to be saved.
source_text: Isti non recte explicant doctrinam reprobationis, qui talem statuunt reprobationem, quae impediat quo minus publicae preces Deo offerri possint cum debita fide et fiducia quod omnibus verbum Dei audientibus sint profutura. Nam quis animum inducere potest ut pro eorum salute oret, quos Deus aeterna et antecedente voluntate damnare voluit? Apostolus hoc argumento nos acuit ad precandum pro omnibus, quia Deus vult omnes salvos fieri.
